claims.text: Acute nasal symptoms: usually no testing, unless invasive sinusitis is suspected in a diabetic or immunocompromised patient (CT, biopsy and histopathology for fungal hyphae).
claims.quote: Testing is generally not indicated for acute nasal symptoms unless invasive sinusitis is suspected in a diabetic or immunocompromised patient; these patients usually require CT, biopsy, and histopathological examination for the presence of fungal hyphae.

claims.text: Acute sinusitis: no imaging unless findings suggest complications, then CT.
claims.quote: Imaging is not indicated in acute sinusitis unless there are findings that suggest complications, in which case CT is performed.

claims.text: Bacterial sinusitis is suspected when purulent rhinorrhea lasts > 10 days with fatigue and cough.
claims.quote: acute (bacterial) sinusitis is suspected when purulent rhinorrhea persists for > 10 days along with fatigue and cough.

claims.text: Cultures only when empiric treatment fails, in immunocompromised patients, and in some hospital-acquired sinusitis.
claims.quote: Cultures are typically performed only when empiric treatment fails, in immunocompromised patients, and in some hospital-acquired causes of sinusitis.

claims.text: Chronic or seasonal symptoms: allergy testing (skin testing or allergen-specific IgE).
claims.quote: In patients with chronic or seasonally recurring nasal symptoms, allergy testing using percutaneous or intradermal skin testing or allergen-specific serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) may help identify an allergic etiology.

claims.text: Suspected CSF leak: test the discharge for beta-2 transferrin.
claims.quote: If a CSF leak is suspected, a sample of the discharge should be tested for the presence of beta-2 transferrin, which is highly specific for CSF.
